collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager proposes a day when anyone can speak about their worries without being judged: hold it, or keep worries private.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has suggested a Day of Listening: once a season, anyone may speak about what worries them, and nobody may interrupt, argue or give advice. (friend) thinks some people will be embarrassed, and that worries belong at home. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The first Day of Listening is awkward. Then an old fisher talks about being afraid of getting too old to fish, and the whole village goes still. More people speak. Nobody gives advice. Everybody listens.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village decides worries belong at home. (subject) starts a small listening circle of (subject.his/her) own, by the lagoon, for anyone who wants it. It grows. (friend) comes, one evening, and sits at the back.
